title: SIGKILL a Chromium tab's renderer: the app stays up, the tab shows the sad tab, and Reload brings the page back
preconditions: a fresh launch: one window, one workspace, one terminal tab
the loopback web fixture serves load.html ($WEB)
the default browser engine is Chromium

allow_crashes.reason: kill-renderer ends the tab's renderer on purpose (the script's renderer case)

expect.noReceiptReason: a CLI run prints the new tab, not the action's receipt

steps.note: a Chromium tab on the fixture page in the focused pane, shown (--focus)

expect.noReceiptReason: a kill step signals a process; no action runs

steps.note: SIGKILL the renderer of the case's only Chromium tab (an exact pid of the app's process tree)
the tab says its page is gone (crashed true); the app runs
Reload (Cmd-R, browserReload) on the tab brings the page back in a new renderer

invariants: converted from scripts/cmux-next/child-crash-e2e.py, which stays as the live check; tests/oracle/corpus/e2e/coverage.json lists the script as blocked: this case moves into tests/oracle/corpus/e2e/ when driver_app.py runs its steps
the app's pid is unchanged: a renderer exit never ends cmux (crash-elimination.md classes 13 and 14)
sad-tab: the tab is crashed and every other value equals loaded's (no other tab, pane or workspace changes)
reloaded: the tab is not crashed and shows $WEB/load.html again; crashes counts one renderer exit only
teardown: quit the tagged app the run started
verify its debug socket is gone
untested: the sad tab's own Reload button (the script presses it through debug.browser.page_status press): Cmd-R runs the browser's reload
a terminal beside the page answering keys through the kill window: that is the crash-survival perf story (key_to_frame)
the WebKit WebContent and agent page kills: their pids come from debug methods (page_pid, debug.agent_pane pid) that no kill target names
